name: weak_constraint_summary
description: The optimality summary must list every weak constraint that can pay at a level, violated or not, with the cost each one pays. The two constraints force a onto day 1 or 2 and b onto day 2 or 3, so the unique optimum is shift(a,1), shift(b,3): level 1 costs 3+2=5 and ':~ shift(N,2).' stays unviolated, while the single constraint of level 2 is not violated because a and b never share a day.
program:
day(1..3).
nurse(a).
nurse(b).
{ shift(N,D) : day(D) } = 1 :- nurse(N).
:- shift(a,3).
:- shift(b,1).
:~ shift(N,1). [3@1,N]
:~ shift(N,2). [5@1,N]
:~ shift(N,3). [2@1,N]
:~ shift(a,D), shift(b,D). [7@2,D]
